# Company portability, end to end

One company (`acme`, the tiny fixture) moved between two checkouts:
exported, recorded under its own id, verified, imported into a clean
tree, and rolled back — with the two refusals an operator actually
meets on the way. The temp path prints as `$TMP`; log timestamps are
normalised, the `bundle-…` id is real because it is content.
Reproduce the whole transcript with:

```
python scripts/portable_walkthrough.py
```

## Export the company

The line carries the three things an operator needs: the id, how many artefacts travel, and the pin it was compiled against beside the platform it is going to.

```
$ bin/portable export --company acme --root $TMP/source --platform contract-2026.11.3
acme  bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d  3 artefact(s)  pinned at contract-2026.11.1  → contract-2026.11.3
```

## Record it

The carrier is stored under its own id: `companies/acme/bundles/bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d/`, with the template beside the manifest.

```
$ bin/portable record --company acme --root $TMP/source --platform contract-2026.11.3
acme  bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d  stored at companies/acme/bundles/bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d
```

## Recording again is silent

The id is the identity, so nothing moved and nothing is written — the metadata in the manifest (`createdAt`, the platform) does not make a second bundle.

```
$ bin/portable record …
acme  bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d  unchanged (already stored)
```

## The history

Newest first, with the action that produced each row.

```
$ bin/portable bundles --company acme --root $TMP/source
acme: 1 stored bundle(s), newest first
  <time>  bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d  3 artefact(s)  export
```

Every artefact by kind, its version, and the first twelve characters of its digest. The company's own files are `org`; the industry's are flows, rules or its pack.

## Verify it against the checkout

Two questions are asked by two things: the carrier's own integrity always, and every artefact's digest where the checkout has the company. This is the second.

```
$ bin/portable verify --bundle $TMP/source/companies/acme/bundles/bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d/bundle.json --root $TMP/source
acme  bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d  verifies
```

## Diff two bundles

Manifest to manifest, per `kind:id`. Two exports of one state differ in nothing, which is what a rollback target must be.

```
$ bin/portable diff --left …/bundle.json --right …/bundle.json
the same bundle
```

## Import into a clean checkout

The target has the model but not the compiled template; the artefacts travel with the bundle, so their absence there is not a fault.

```
$ bin/portable import --bundle $TMP/handover/bundle.json --root $TMP/import --platform contract-2026.11.3
acme  bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d  imported → companies/acme/paperclip-company.json
```

## The same id on the other side

`bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d` again: the two checkouts agree the company is the same, because the id is content and nothing about the move changed the content.

```
$ bin/portable record --company acme --root $TMP/import --platform contract-2026.11.3
acme  bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d  stored at companies/acme/bundles/bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d
```

## A bundle newer than the platform is refused

`E-PORT-06`: the importer must not silently drop what it cannot read. The opposite direction — an older bundle into a newer platform — is allowed and recorded.

```
$ bin/portable export --company acme --root $TMP/source --platform contract-2026.09.0
portable: E-PORT-06: the bundle is pinned at contract-2026.11.1 and the platform is contract-2026.09.0 — fix: upgrade the platform first; the importer must not silently drop what it cannot read
(exit 1)
```

## A bundle that carries tenant data is refused

`E-PORT-05`: a company bundle is the org, never a tenant's documents. A business leaving with another business's papers is not portability.

```
$ bin/portable export --company acme --root $TMP/import --platform contract-2026.11.3
portable: E-PORT-05: 'customers/acme/org.json' is tenant data — fix: strip it; company portability never moves a tenant's documents
(exit 1)
```

## A rollback that would overwrite is refused

`E-PORT-04`: a rollback replaces a live compiled model, so it is deliberate. The refusal is the feature.

```
$ bin/portable rollback --company acme --to bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d --root $TMP/import
portable: E-PORT-08: rolling back to bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d would overwrite companies/acme/paperclip-company.json — fix: pass --force if that is what you mean; a rollback replaces a compiled model, so it is deliberate and it is logged
(exit 1)
```

## And --force does it, on the record

The log gets a `rollback` row naming what it restored, and the checkout re-exports to the same id it went back to — which makes the id a proof of the restore, not a label.

```
$ bin/portable rollback --company acme --to bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d --root $TMP/import --force
acme  rolled back to bundle-7428f5cbc337d64d (forced)  → companies/acme/paperclip-company.json
```

## Check the store

Every stored carrier against its own manifest, every directory named by its bundle id, every log row naming a carrier that exists.

```
$ bin/portable check --root $TMP/import
portable: 1 stored bundle(s) verify
```

## What the run shows

* A bundle is the template plus everything it names, and its id is
  the digest of exactly that — so two exports of one state are one
  bundle, and a re-record writes nothing.
* Three refusals protect the *scope*: tenant data, a newer contract,
  and an absolute path. None of them is a warning.
* A rollback is an import of a stored id, made deliberate: it needs
  `--force` to overwrite, and it leaves a row saying it happened.
* The company's own files are `org`; an industry's are flows, rules
  or its pack. A repo-shipped artefact is versioned by the pin it
  ships with unless the file declares its own.
